item.title: Causal Information Exchange as a Necessary Condition for Adaptive Regulation: A Perturbational Framework for Life and Agency
item.description: arXiv:2610.24017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Information exchange can support living organisation without providing a sufficient criterion for life. We develop a perturbational framework that distinguishes causal transmission, directional imbalance, internal retention, response structure and functional regulation. Randomised interventions define Shannon information channels; for deterministic binary recipients, their context-conditioned mutual information is exactly a paired perturbation-response indicator. Spatial and temporal averages of these local channels measure information-exposure density, rather than joint information or conserved information flux. Complementary Coding Theorem Method and Block Decomposition Method (BDM) estimates describe response and trajectory structure. A same-shaped zero-mask reference separates raw BDM from a structural contrast; neither is a channel mutual information. Retained exploratory BDM plots are distinguished from the normalised causal-channel results. Retention-weighted coupling and directionality obey algebraic bounds, and ensemble reciprocity need not imply reciprocity within individual contexts. For a specified binary sensor--internal-channel--actuator task, we derive a positive information lower bound from successful regulation and construct controllers with identical information profiles but opposite functional outcomes. A study of 2,000 ordered elementary-cellular-automaton rule pairs, six detailed examples, recurrence and lossless coding analyses, and a signed-network extension demonstrates dissociations among perturbational responsiveness, structural regularity and recurrence. The results establish causal information as a necessary resource for the stated form of adaptive regulation, while showing why neither causal coupling nor response complexity alone measures agency or life.
item.dc:creator: Brian LuValle, Abicumaran Uthamacumaran, Hector Zenil

item.title: Explicit construction of optimal binary linear complementary pairs via Belov codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The study of linear complementary pairs (LCPs) has been a hot topic in coding theory. Recently, G\"uneri constructed an infinite family of optimal binary LCPs from Solomon-Stiffler codes. Specifically, he proved that for every $k \geq 5$ and $d \geq \lceil (k - 1)/2 \rceil 2^{k - 1}$, there exist optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes of length $g_2(k,d)$, where $g_2(k,d)$ denotes the Griesmer bound. In this paper, we construct additional optimal binary LCPs from Belov codes, which form a generalized class of Solomon-Stiffler codes. Our results not only generalize G\"uneri's construction, but also enable more flexible construction of optimal binary LCPs with a wide range of minimum distances.
item.dc:creator: Yansheng Wu, Jing Chen, Jong Yoon Hyun

item.title: Representing Information on DNA using Patterns Induced by Enzymatic Labeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.24171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enzymatic DNA labeling is a powerful tool with applications in biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, medical science, and genomic research. This paper contributes to the evolving field of DNA-based data storage by presenting a formal framework for modeling DNA labeling in strings, specifically tailored for data storage purposes. Our approach involves a known DNA molecule as a template for labeling, employing patterns induced by a set of designed labels to represent information. One hypothetical implementation can use CRISPR-Cas9 and gRNA reagents for labeling. Various aspects of the general labeling channel, including fixed-length labels, are explored, and upper bounds on the maximum size of the corresponding codes are given. The study includes the development of an efficient encoder-decoder pair that is proven to be optimal in terms of maximum code size under specific conditions. The codewords for this framework are codesets, i.e., each codeword is a collection of a few labels. Of special interest are codes whose codesets contain fixed-length labels. Their construction and analysis are tied to de Bruijn sequences and constrained coding.
item.dc:creator: Daniella Bar-Lev, Eitan Yaakobi, Zohar Yakhini, Tuvi Etzion

item.title: Orientation Diversity Provably Increases the Angular-Domain Rank of 3D MIMO Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.24228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable and rotatable-antenna systems treat element placement as a design resource, but the supporting theory is largely position-only. We prove that element orientation is an effective spatial resource in its own right, complementary to position. For collinear or coplanar arrays, the angular-domain rank is capped by the number of projection-ambiguity classes of the scattering directions, for every common element orientation and pattern. Orientation-diverse elements with sufficiently rich analytic patterns restore the maximal rank min(N,L) for almost every orientation draw. A closed-form correlation expression, strictly monotone in orientation spread under isotropic scattering, quantifies the gain within the scalar-pattern model, and Monte Carlo simulations corroborate the exact-rank and capacity behavior.
item.dc:creator: Samer Henry, Elvino Sousa

item.title: Pilot-Projected Nonlinear Self-Interference Estimation with Simultaneous Uplink Training
item.description: arXiv:2610.24243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers nonlinear digital self-interference (SI) cancellation and uplink-channel estimation for single-antenna in-band full-duplex radios when a desired uplink pilot is present during SI training. In this setting, a rich nonlinear SI dictionary can absorb part of the structured pilot response, while its large and correlated set of basis functions can make reliable SI estimation difficult, particularly with limited training. During SI-coefficient estimation, we treat the unknown uplink channel as a nuisance parameter and eliminate it to obtain an equivalent reduced SI estimation problem on the orthogonal complement of the pilot convolution subspace. Since the projected nonlinear dictionary can remain ill conditioned, we develop two complementary full-dictionary estimators: a pilot-projected ridge estimator with Bayesian-information-criterion tuning (PP-RidgeBIC), which uses global ridge shrinkage, and a pilot-projected group-sparse Bayesian estimator (PP-GSBE), which learns branch-dependent Bayesian shrinkage from the data. These estimators offer two complementary operating points: PP-RidgeBIC favors computational efficiency, whereas PP-GSBE provides greater adaptivity to heterogeneous nonlinear SI components. Simulations show substantial gains in SI cancellation and uplink reception over non-projected and hard-selection alternatives; notably, PP-GSBE suppresses the residual SI below the noise floor with moderate training and consistently provides the strongest performance under nonlinear model mismatch.
item.dc:creator: Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi, Thomas Eriksson

item.title: Information Theory of Random Composition Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.24788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random composition trees model the hierarchical semantic structures of meaningful texts as a statistical ensemble generated by recursively splitting texts into coherent chunks. A recent study shows that different text types can be described by random composition trees with distinct branching factors, and that the entropy rates of these trees exhibit a similar dependence across text types as the entropy rates of the actual texts. Motivated by this correspondence, we analyze information-theoretic properties of this stochastic splitting model. First, we demonstrate that the entropy of random composition trees grows linearly with the root size, and we derive an analytical expression for the entropy rate as a function of the branching factor. Second, we prove that large trees exhibit typicality: with high probability, they belong to a typical set in which each tree is approximately equally likely. Our analysis reveals that the random composition tree model shares two key information-theoretic properties of language when modeled as a stationary and ergodic stochastic process: linear entropy growth and typicality.
item.dc:creator: Doron Sivan, Weishun Zhong, Tankut Can, Mikhail Katkov, Misha Tsodyks

item.title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate budgets. In the static bit-probe model [Yao, 1981], an encoder stores $w$ bits about $x$ before seeing a query $y$, and a reader probes at most $r<w$ bits to estimate $x^\top y$. Both vectors lie in the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Protocols may be randomized, and computation is unrestricted. Performance is measured by $d$ times the worst-case mean-squared error over $x,y$, averaged over protocol randomness. First, we show that query-independent reading cannot benefit from extra storage. Any such reader is equivalent to fully reading an $r$-bit message, even when later reads depend on previously returned bits. At fixed positive rates $W=w/d$ and $R=r/d$, the normalized minimax error converges to $1/(4^R-1)$, independent of $W$. The upper bound was already known [Ordentlich and Polyanskiy, 2025]. We prove the matching lower bound for arbitrary scalar decoders, extending the result for unbiased compressors [Safaryan et al., 2020]. Then, we show that query-dependent reading makes extra storage useful. We construct a two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds, with asymptotic normalized error at most $(\pi+o(1))/[4R\log(W/R)]$ as $W/R\to\infty$. At fixed $R$, this error vanishes as storage grows, giving an unbounded advantage over query-independent reading. We also prove a finite-dimensional lower bound for arbitrary encoders, decoders, and fully branching readers. In the doubly sparse regime $W/R\to\infty$ and $R\log(W/R)\to0$, it gives normalized error at least $(1-o(1))/[2R\log(W/R)]$. Thus, our protocol is optimal within a factor of $\pi/2$ in the leading constant.
item.dc:creator: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Siddharth Bhandari, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan

item.title: Convergence of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models: A R\'{e}nyi Divergence Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2610.24984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling by transforming standard Gaussian inputs into outputs that approximate a target distribution. While DDPMs have been proved to converge in total variation, KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance, these discrepancy measures share a fundamental limitation of being insensitive to distributional mismatch in low-probability regions. To address this, we adopt the stronger R\'enyi divergence as the discrepancy measure. Leveraging a Girsanov-type change-of-measure argument, we establish the first R\'enyi characterization of DDPMs to the best of our knowledge, showing that the total error decomposes into a mixing error, a discretization error, and a score estimation error. We assume the target distribution is sub-Gaussian and characterize the score error via the cumulant generating function, relaxing both the log-Sobolev-inequality and $L^\infty$-score-error conditions used in prior R\'enyi divergence analyses of inexact Langevin Monte Carlo, a score-based sampling algorithm closely related to DDPM. Our results also establish an iteration complexity for achieving $\epsilon$-accuracy in $\alpha$-R\'enyi divergence that is asymptotically proportional to $\alpha^3/\epsilon$. Finally, by extending our analysis, we establish the first R\'enyi divergence convergence guarantee for critically damped DDPMs, a kinetic variant governed by critically damped Langevin dynamics. Similar to existing characterizations of critically damped DDPMs, this result shares the structural scaling of standard DDPMs, differing by at most a logarithmic factor in the mixing error exponent, and supports the conjecture that critically damped DDPMs do not yield a theoretical improvement.
item.dc:creator: Wenliang Liu, Santiago Mazuelas, Guanding Yu, Renjie Liao, Lele Wang, Yuan Shen

item.title: A Self-Coupling Gaussian Extremal Inequality for Information-Constrained Optimal Transport with Applications to Rate-Distortion-Perception
item.description: arXiv:2610.25041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much mutual information is needed to achieve a target correlation between two copies of a prescribed distribution? We prove a sharp Gaussian extremal inequality for this self-coupling problem: among distributions with a fixed mean and covariance, the Gaussian has the greatest minimum information cost for meeting a positive semidefinite cross-covariance target. The inequality is strict for non-Gaussian distributions when the target is positive definite. The proof uses a midpoint gluing construction. Two Ornstein--Uhlenbeck half-bridges, each started from the prescribed endpoint law, meet at a common intermediate distribution and are joined by conditional gluing. Changing the Gaussian reference then turns the resulting relative-entropy bound into the desired extremal inequality. As a first application, scaling one endpoint of the self-coupling establishes Gaussian extremality for rate-distortion-perception with unlimited common randomness, under quadratic distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures. We also establish an analogous result for finite common randomness, where the problem involves two mutual information constraints associated with an auxiliary random variable. In that setting, we retain an intermediate observation on one half-bridge and balance the two information budgets simultaneously using the Poincar\'{e}-Miranda theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jiayang Zou, Jun Chen, Ayfer \"{O}zg\"{u}r, Jia Wang

item.title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2610.25098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent can retain information before receiving a future question and later retrieve evidence from an archive. Evaluating this arrangement requires accounting for both retained information and the width of each retrieval response. Decision-tree capacity bounds describe individual sets of distinguishable records, but a memory writer must encode every possible record before the query is known. We study fixed-length retention beside an immutable binary archive, with a worst-case limit on raw bit or word reads. We characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells and construct encoders that partition the complete record space. Supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query. For multiple reads, we combine explicit encoders with decision-tree counting and an entropy converse. The word-read bounds differ by at most two retained bits when the read budget is at most half the archive length. Under an explicit condition on word width and archive length, raw-word caching attains the exact optimum among all writers. A related condition preserves this optimum under positive average error. Exhaustive checks validate the implementations. In a matched dialogue-agent study, a categorical sufficient statistic preserves source decisions with less storage and lower decoding latency than the universal encoder. A catalogue-specific index reduces private state further and requires additional shared storage. The results characterize how response width and future query structure determine retention requirements.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Singh, Prashant Singh

item.title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.25490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.
item.dc:creator: Chao Tian, Krishna Narayanan

item.title: PMR-Aided Shifted-Pruning SCL-Flip Decoding for CRC-Aided Polar Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.25644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a posterior-mass rescue (PMR)-aided shifted-pruning SCL-flip decoder for CRC-aided polar codes. After CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) and differential-metric shifted-pruning recovery fail to find a CRC-valid candidate, PMR locally continues discarded prefixes stored during the initial CA-SCL pass, ranked by estimated posterior mass, without increasing the shifted-pruning retry budget. Simulation results for a (128, 64) code with the Reed-Muller (RM) rate profile and a (256, 128) code with the polarization-weight (PW) rate profile, both using an 11-bit CRC, show lower observed FER than SCLF-Diff (T = 15) and the considered literature baselines under the evaluated recovery budgets, with observed FER close to that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20). At the reported moderate and high SNRs, the average reconstruction-aware path-step count is within a few percent of that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20), while at 2.0 dB it is 9.4% and 4.3% higher for the two codes, respectively. The proposed decoder also has a larger worst-case path-step bound.
item.dc:creator: Niloufar Hosseinzadeh, Mohammad Morsali, Mohsen Moradi, Hessam Mahdavifar

item.title: Fundamental Limits of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation with User Dropouts in Federated Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.25743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of users' gradients or model updates without revealing individual values. With user dropouts, correlated random keys protect local gradients while allowing recovery of the desired gradient sum. We consider three phases: key distribution, masked-gradient upload, and mask elimination. Users establish correlated keys, upload masked gradients, and provide additional messages to eliminate residual aggregate masks. Existing information-theoretic schemes typically design mask-elimination communication for a prescribed dropout threshold and evaluate its cost under worst-case dropouts across the masked-gradient upload and mask-elimination phases. Such designs cannot adjust communication to actual dropout scenarios. Moreover, the randomness and communication costs of establishing correlated keys remain largely unexplored. To address these limitations, we formulate an adaptive secure aggregation framework under the T-colluding security constraint and construct a single scheme that supports all feasible dropout scenarios by adapting its communication to the actual number of dropouts. We establish converse bounds on four resources: key randomness, key-distribution communication, masked-gradient communication, and mask-elimination communication. The latter two bounds are characterized for each realized dropout set in the masked-gradient upload phase. The proposed scheme achieves the optimal masked-gradient communication rate for every feasible dropout scenario and the optimal mask-elimination communication rate in almost all feasible regimes. Its key rate and key-distribution communication rate are each optimal or within a factor of two of their respective information-theoretic optima. These results characterize the fundamental randomness and communication costs of secure aggregation with user dropouts.
item.dc:creator: Jinbao Zhu, Kai Wan, Giuseppe Caire

item.title: Finite BSC-Decomposition of Binary-Input Symmetric-Output Channels and Applications to Channel Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a finite BSC-decomposition method for representing an arbitrary binary-input symmetric-output channel (BISOC) as a mixture of binary symmetric channels (BSCs) with at most $\ell+1$ distinct crossover probabilities. We show that the weighted average capacity of the component BSCs exceeds the capacity of the original BISOC by at most $(\pi^2\log e)/(48\ell^2)+O(\ell^{-5/2})$ bits, and the leading term is asymptotically optimal in the worst case. Based on the finite BSC-decomposition, we design a channel simulation scheme for arbitrary BISOCs. Combined with efficient channel simulation algorithms for BSCs, our scheme achieves a communication rate with $O((\log n / n)^{2/3})$ redundancy over the capacity for simulating $n$ copies of a BISOC.
item.dc:creator: Jianguo Zhao, Cheuk Ting Li

item.title: On the Information Bottleneck for Ergodic Finite-State Markov Chains: Stationary Approximation and Asymptotic Optimality
item.description: arXiv:2610.25952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the information bottleneck problem for sources that follow discrete-time ergodic finite-state Markov chains. We propose treating observations generated by the time-varying Markov chain as if they were drawn from its unique stationary distribution, and we use the solution to the information bottleneck problem for the stationary process to compress samples from the time-varying process. The resulting error is upper bounded by several information gap terms. We establish sufficient conditions under which these gaps converge to zero and analyze the convergence rates of the different information gap terms. The proofs are based on intricate analysis using convergence of subsequences along with the derivation of properties of the optimization sets associated with the information bottleneck problem. In addition to the inequalities and convergence results we establish, our analysis offers insights into how simple properties of ergodic Markov chains give rise to results concerning the information bottleneck problem for such chains.
item.dc:creator: Wael Tabbara, Jihad Fahs, Mohamad Assaad

item.title: On the Adaptive Covering Complexity of Strings: Unifying Relative and Self-Referential Compression
item.description: arXiv:2610.26021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the adaptive covering complexity C adapt S (s), defined as the minimum number of contiguous factor blocks required to partition a string s when each block is either a factor of a fixed external dictionary S or a factor of the target's already decoded prefix. This hybrid admissibility model formalizes the structural interaction between static dictionary matching and dynamic nonoverlapping self-referencing. Our main theoretical result is the exact logarithmic law which is tight and proves that dynamic self-reference can reduce phrase count by at most an exponential factor over static dictionary covering alone. We establish structural equivalences showing that the measure bridges word-segmented Relative Lempel-Ziv and non-overlapping LZ77, and we prove exact preset-history LZ77 sandwich bounds. Furthermore, we establish the optimality of the longest-match greedy parse via an exchange lemma and present an optimal implementation based on dual suffix automata running in O(M + n) time and space for a constant alphabet. These analytical results are complemented by counting bounds, stationary-ergodic asymptotic invariance, a dictionaryselection NP-hardness result, and a concise empirical illustration.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Fran{\c c}ois Marteau (EXPRESSION)

item.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Santonastaso, Yue Zhou

item.title: A Hyperplane Bound and Ward's Divisibility Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q=p^f$, where $p$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-ary linear code meeting the Griesmer bound, with positive dimension and minimum distance $d\ge1$, is $p^{\max\{0,\nu_p(d)-f+1\}}$-divisible, as asserted in Ward's conjecture. Arbitrary projective column multiplicities are allowed. The geometric ingredient is a bound independent of dimension: a nonzero scalar-invariant function $F:\mathbb{F}_q^k\to\mathbb{F}_p$, with $F(0)=0$ and prime-field algebraic degree at most $(f+s)(p-1)$, vanishes identically on at most $p^s(q-1)$ linear hyperplanes when $0\le s<f$. A truncated digit-sum inequality forces selected coefficient polynomials to be homogeneous of ordinary degree less than $q$. Weighted moments on a projective line then bound their linear factors, while a second-moment argument handles the complementary support configuration. An elementary finite-difference calculation supplies the degree bound for divided weight residues. Endpoint shortenings prove the basic divisibility layers; endpoint lifting, a surjective linear functional, and residual-code induction extend the argument to every valuation. We include the proofs of the classical ingredients, identify their sources, and distinguish the present argument from an earlier reported unpublished proof.
item.dc:creator: Guanghui Zhang

item.title: Corrections to ``The Method of Gaps: Exact Expressions for the Generalization Error of Supervised Learning Algorithms''
item.description: arXiv:2610.26245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a counterexample to Lemma 5 of the paper referenced in the title is provided. Consequently, the formulation of the method of data-driven gaps presented in the referenced paper relies on an additional assumption, namely, that the conditional distribution of the training dataset given the learned model has identical data-point-specific marginals. To overcome this limitation, a generalized formulation of the method of data-driven gaps that does not rely on Lemma 5 and does not require the training samples to be independent or identically distributed is presented. Through this formulation, the applicability of the method of data-driven gaps is extended to a broader class of data distributions and randomized learning algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Samir M. Perlaza (NEO,ECE,GAATI)

item.title: Basis Selection For Analog Coded Computing Under Differential Privacy Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.26385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In analog coded computing, encoding basis functions are typically chosen to guarantee exact reconstruction and improve numerical stability. However, the same basis functions also determine the statistical geometry of the observations available to colluding workers, and hence directly influence the privacy of the underlying data. This suggests that basis selection should not be viewed solely as a reconstruction or numerical conditioning problem, but rather as a joint privacy and accuracy co-design problem. Motivated by this observation, we revisit Analog Lagrange Coded Computing (ALCC) and show that the full orthogonality constraints imposed by the conventional Lagrange basis are stronger than what is required for exact recovery. We retain only the interpolation constraints necessary for the data bearing basis functions and require the noise bearing basis functions merely to vanish at the data recovery points. This yields a parameterized family of generalized polynomial encoding bases that preserves exact reconstruction while introducing additional design degrees of freedom. We then derive a basis-dependent characterization of differential privacy for colluding workers and formulate a privacy-calibrated numerical optimization problem that jointly selects the data and noise basis functions to reduce reconstruction error while satisfying a prescribed \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-DP requirement. The resulting framework therefore treats the encoding basis itself as a privacy-design variable, rather than selecting a fixed closed-form basis a priori. The same design philosophy is also compatible with alternative privacy metrics such as mutual-information leakage. Numerical results show that, at the same privacy level, optimized basis functions substantially reduce floating-point reconstruction error relative to conventional ALCC.
item.dc:creator: Aaditya Sharma, Rimpi Borah, J. Harshan

item.title: Universal coding with the exhaustive peres transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.26396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peres's iteration of von Neumann's procedure is completed into a bijection of $\bits^N$: the recursion runs to exhaustion, nothing is discarded, and every input splits into fair bits and residual bits. The residual strings form a complete prefix code that determines the number of ones of the input, so the fair bits are exactly uniform given the residual for every exchangeable law. For a Bernoulli source the likelihood factorises exactly, in decoding order, into a factor $1/2$ per fair bit and a Bernoulli factor per residual bit, with biases obtained by iterating two explicit maps. The number of fair bits per input symbol tends to the entropy almost surely, also on larger alphabets. Code B stores the fair bits and codes only the residual with an arithmetic coder; its ideal length is that of the two-part code, at most $\log\_2(N+1)+1$ bits above $-\log\_2\Pr\_\theta(s)$ for every input $s$ and bias $\theta$. Code C uses Rice codes instead. In experiments up to $N=2^{20}$ its mean regret stays below $200$ bits, where a Rice coder on the raw input loses a fixed fraction of the entropy on skewed sources. For sources with memory, the Burrows--Wheeler transform of the reversed string arranges all context orders in one tree of intervals; coding the leaves of a pruned tree as Bernoulli strings adapts to every Markov order up to its depth, and on suffix-closed trees the leaf weights determine the split points.
item.dc:creator: Aur{\'e}lien Garivier (UMPA-ENSL,MC2)

item.title: On True Minimum Distances of Goppa Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary Goppa codes are important in coding theory and cryptography. It is well-known that the minimum distance of a binary Goppa code defined by a squarefree polynomial of degree $r$ is at least $2r+1$. Though from the classical results of C. J. Moreno, O. Moreno, F. Levy-dit-Vehel and S. Litsyn that the true minimum distances of binary Goppa codes are $2r+1$, when the extension field degree $m$ is larger than $(r-1)^{4r}$. There have only very few families of binary Goppa codes with determined true minimum distances. In this paper, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for binary Goppa codes such that their minimum distances are $2r+1$ and $2r+2$. Infinitely many infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance $2r+1$ are given. In particular, we construct such codes for every Goppa degree $r$ in the range $2^{h-1}<r<2^h$ over $\mathbb F_{2^{2h}}$. For every $2\le r\le\lfloor2^m/3\rfloor$, we also obtain at least $2^m-3r+1$ distinct monic squarefree Goppa polynomials of degree $r$ over $\mathbb F_{2^m}$, such that their related binary Goppa codes have minimum distance $2r+1$. We extend a criterion for $q$-ary Goppa codes to split auxiliary polynomials and obtain some infinite families of $q$-ary Goppa codes attaining their designed distances $r+1$. We also construct infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance exactly $2r+2$.
item.dc:creator: Yaqi Chen, Hao Chen, Chao Liu, Huimin Lao

item.title: A study of the $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances with a special emphasis on $C_{ab}$ curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.26649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the seminal paper [13], Farr\'an and Munuera introduced a method to establish generic information on the $m$th Feng-Rao distance via a function on arbitrary numerical semigroups that serves as a lower bound on the generalized Hamming weights of dual one-point algebraic geometry codes whenever the semigroup is Weierstrass. In the present paper, we study what we shall call the primary and dual, respectively, $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances, which serve as lower bounds on relative generalized Hamming weights of nested primary and dual, respectively, one-point codes under similar condition. A unified method for establishing generic formulas for $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances of general numerical semigroups is developed and for a large variety of numerical semigroups generated by two elements, closed formula expressions are established complementing Delgado et al.s work [8] on the $m$th Feng-Rao distances of such semigroups. Finally, for non-singular $C_{ab}$ curves, we develop a method to estimate the $m$th relative generalized Hamming weight of dual and primary one-point codes in those regions where the generic methods may fail to provide best possible results.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Camps-Moreno, Olav Geil, Hiram H. L\'opez, Gretchen L. Matthews, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e

item.title: Bounds on the Service Rates of Linear Codes and their Connections to Combinatorial Designs
item.description: arXiv:2610.26683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The service rate region of a distributed storage system describes the set of concurrent demand vectors that can be served without overloading any individual server, and is a fundamental measure of how effectively redundancy is used. In this paper, we investigate aggregate service rates in distributed data storage systems based on linear codes over arbitrary finite fields. We first derive an upper bound on the aggregate service rate for an arbitrary subset of $t$ data objects in terms of the dual distance and the sizes of their smallest recovery sets. For systematic generator matrices, this bound simplifies to an expression depending only on the code length, the dual distance, and the cardinality of the selected subset. This result extends existing bounds and provides a subset-wise formulation of the First Dual Distance Bound. We then establish conditions under which this upper bound is attained. We apply our results to several important families of linear codes, including MDS codes, Reed-Muller codes, constacyclic codes, and extended Golay codes, and obtain exact values of the maximum aggregate service rates for the corresponding subsets of data objects.
item.dc:creator: Monika Yadav, Priyanka Choudhary, Maheshanand Bhaintwal

item.title: Block basis reduction for linear codes in non-Hamming metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.26808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we generalize the code basis reduction to non-Hamming metrics. We propose a block basis reduction (BKZ) algorithm for codes that works for all coordinate-additive metrics. Our algorithm is a generalization of the algorithm of Ghentiyala and Stephens-Davidowitz, which in turn is an adaptation of the famous BKZ algorithm for lattices to linear codes and the Hamming metric. For block size~$2$ (LLL), we propose a polynomial-time algorithm with complexity~$\mathcal{O}(n^4 q^3)$ operations in~$\mathbb{F}_q$, where~$n$ is the length of the code and~$q$ is the alphabet size. For the Lee metric we provide an implementation of our algorithms and present experimental results on finding low Lee weight codewords.
item.dc:creator: N. S. Kolesnikov, S. A. Novoselov

item.title: Scattering Measures and Information Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.34721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate scattering experiments in terms of parameterized finite measures on outcome spaces and develop the associated information geometry defined by the Fisher metric. The decomposition of a scattering measure into total mass and normalized shape separates Fisher information into contributions from changes in overall scattering strength and redistribution among outcomes. Measurement processes are represented by probability or sub-probability kernels acting on the scattering measure. Such kernels contract Fisher information, placing a broad class of experimental operations within a common information-theoretic framework. This formulation connects scattering experiments to the theory of optimal experimental design through the Fisher geometry of scattering measures. The same finite-measure structure arises naturally in quantum measurements with incomplete detection, clarifying its place in the hierarchy from quantum measurement to classical outcome statistics.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuro Oda

item.title: Asymmetric Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) permit reconstruction of a lost coordinate from a small subset of the remaining coordinates, a property that is a fundamental coding technique for distributed storage and, more recently, for fault-tolerant quantum memories and distributed storage systems. Existing constructions of quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) and their entanglement-assisted generalizations (EA-qLRCs) impose a single locality parameter $r$ governing recovery from both bit-flip ($X$-type) and phase-flip ($Z$-type) errors, even though physical noise is rarely symmetric between the two. We introduce entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes (EA-qLRC) with \emph{asymmetric locality} $\{r_X,r_Z\}$, in which $X$-type and $Z$-type errors are corrected from recovery sets of size at most $r_X+1$ and $r_Z+1$, respectively. We extend a stabilizer sufficient condition for this property and, in particular, the CSS framework, where asymmetric locality corresponds to separate locality conditions on the two classical codes $\mathcal C_1$ and $\mathcal C_2$ underlying the construction. From this characterization we derive Singleton-, Griesmer-, Plotkin-, sphere-packing-, and Cadambe\textendash Mazumdar-like bounds for CSS-type asymmetric EA-qLRCs (AEA-qLRCs) built from Proposition~\ref{CSS-EA-qLRC-Asym}, and we characterize exactly when a pure CSS-type AEA-qLRC built from a pair of classical LRCs attains the Singleton-like bound with equality.
item.dc:creator: Vijay Kumar, Ramakrishna Bandi

item.title: New lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes from prescribed-automorphism search, and two quantum codes meeting their upper bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit binary constant-weight codes that raise the lower bounds on $A(n,6,w)$ in eight cells of Brouwer's table, all now listed there. The first round (9 October 2026) gave four values: $A(27,6,11)\ge 19305$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24453$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 18642$ and $A(28,6,9)\ge 11154$, together with an explicit $A(24,6,12)$ code of 5566 words, now in the table's list of lost codes. The second round (14 October 2026) gave seven values, listed in the table since 15 October 2026: $A(29,6,10)\ge 27183$, $A(29,6,11)\ge 42042$, $A(29,6,9)\ge 14781$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 19110$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24804$, $A(28,6,9)\ge 11388$ and $A(27,6,13)\ge 27783$, three of which replace first-round values. Every code is a union of orbits of the semilinear affine group $\mathrm{A\Gamma L}(1,27)$, its index-2 subgroup, or $\mathrm{AGL}(1,23)$, acting on all but at most two coordinates. The orbits were chosen by maximum-weight independent set search on the orbit conflict graph: branch and bound in the first round, iterated local search in the second. Each code was checked by two separately written programs over all pairs of words and was regenerated from its generators and orbit representatives. We also report two qubit stabilizer codes, $[[20,11,4]]$ and $[[43,32,4]]$, which raise the lower bounds of 3 listed at codetables.de to the listed upper bound 4.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dzoba

item.title: Private Evaluation of High-Dimensional Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study differentially private black-box evaluation of arbitrary high-dimensional functions. Given a dataset $S$ and query access to a function $f$---whose sensitivity may be unknown or unbounded---the goal is to privately output an approximation to $f(S)$. The black-box evaluator can only query the value of $f$ over a down neighborhood of $S$ (i.e., those subsets of $S$ that are obtained by removing a bounded number of elements from $S$). We design generic black-box evaluators for both pure and approximate differential privacy through a reduction to high-dimensional private quasi-concave optimization (QCO). Our black-box evaluator enjoys a geometric notion of utility. Consider the vectors obtained by applying $f$ on sets in a down neighborhood of $S$. With high probability, the evaluator's output is guaranteed to be in the convex hull of these vectors. Our work generalizes the result of Linder et al. [LRSS25] for real-valued function evaluation to high dimensions. It also recovers the private center-point guarantees of Beimel et al. [BMNS19], with an explicit additive approximation to maximum Tukey depth. We also apply our evaluators to user-level quasi-concave and convex optimization, showing how they can improve upon the sample-and-aggregate baseline of Nissim et al. [NRS07] by replacing the multiplicative data overhead with an additive overhead. Finally, we show that our formulation of high dimensional black-box evaluation and high dimensional private QCO are equivalent up to a factor of the dimension: the hardest private evaluation instances already arise from the cases that $f$ is a (non-private) quasi-concave optimizer.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Afzali, Hassan Ashtiani, Adam Smith

item.title: Discrete Phase-Shift Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces using Uniform Reference Directions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) enable programmable control of the wireless propagation environment through adjustable reflecting elements. A fundamental challenge in RIS-assisted communications is the optimization of discrete phase shifts to maximize the received signal power. While recently developed algorithms can obtain optimal solutions with linear complexity, their computational cost may still be excessive in applications requiring large-scale simulations, real-time adaptation, or repeated optimization over numerous channel realizations. This paper proposes a low-complexity discrete phase-shift optimization algorithm based on multiple reference directions within the feasible optimality sector. By evaluating candidate phase configurations generated from uniformly distributed reference directions, the proposed method systematically improves upon existing approximation approaches that rely on a fixed set of reference directions. The number of reference directions serves as a design parameter that enables a controllable trade-off between computational complexity and optimality. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves substantial computational speedups while maintaining a small optimality gap relative to the optimal solution. The results further show that increasing the number of reference directions progressively reduces the optimality gap, providing flexible operating points that can be tailored to application-specific complexity and performance requirements.
item.dc:creator: Pavithra P., Manoj Kumar Panda, Chandramani Singh

item.title: Spectra of Multivariate Vandermonde Matrices and Min-max Error Bounds for the High-dimensional Super-resolution Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.24670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study multivariate rectangular Vandermonde matrices $U_N$ whose rows are indexed by the grid $G_N=\{-N,\ldots,N\}^d, $ and whose columns correspond to irregularly spaced points on the unit $d$-dimensional torus. Motivated by the problem of super-resolution (recovery of spike trains from low frequency noisy measurements), we consider configurations in which the points form several clusters, with points within each cluster separated by at most $h$ and distinct clusters are well-separated. We show that the column subspaces associated with different clusters are nearly orthogonal, i.e. for $N \rightarrow \infty, Nh \ll 1$, the minimal principal angle between any such pair is at least $ {\pi \over 2} - \frac{C_1}{N} - C_2Nh - \frac{C_3}{\sqrt{N}}, $ for some constants $C_1,C_2,C_3$ independent of $N$ and $h$. This near-orthogonality enables the spectral analysis of such $U_N$ to be reduced to the analysis of each individual cluster. As a consequence, we derive sharp scaling for all singular values of $U_N$, revealing how the geometry of clustered points controls the conditioning of the high-dimensional super-resolution problems. Then we establish min-max error bounds for the recovery of clustered point sources, requiring only an upper bound on the largest cluster size and no knowledge of the geometry within the clusters. These bounds coincide with the optimal rates known in the one-dimensional setting. Furthermore, when the clustered points are in generic position (i.e. do not lie on a low-dimensional algebraic variety) our results indicate that super-resolution in high dimensions is more stable than in one dimension.
item.dc:creator: Nuha Diab, Dmitry Batenkov

item.title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A single-track Gray code of length $n$ is a cyclic Gray code of $n$-bit words in which every column is a cyclic shift of the first. For prime $n$ the longest possible period is $2^n-2$. Whether it is attained for every prime has been open since Hiltgen, Paterson and Brandestini introduced these codes in 1996, and optimal codes were known for primes $n\le 19$. We show that a conjecture of Degni and Drisko (2007) on the reflected Gray code order of necklaces implies optimal single-track Gray codes for every prime. Their list of necklaces, conjecturally a Gray path for prime $n$, closes into a Hamilton cycle of the necklace graph after $(n-3)/2$ explicit P\'osa rotations, and such a cycle lifts to an optimal code. This implication is formalized in Lean 4. Together with computation it gives optimal single-track Gray codes for every odd prime $n\le 47$: for $n\le 37$ explicit codes checked word by word by a program independent of the generator, and for $n=41$, $43$ and $47$ codes obtained from the implication after the Degni-Drisko property was verified at these lengths by two independently written programs.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dzoba

item.title: Sample complexity of weak-signal latent-variable models
item.description: arXiv:2610.24770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study parametric estimation in latent-variable models in the weak-signal regime, where a small signal-strength parameter $\beta$ controls the dependence of the observations on the unknown parameter. At $\beta=0$, this dependence disappears, so all parameter values induce the same observed distribution, which we call the null law. We develop a unified framework for analyzing sample complexity in the weak-signal regime by expanding the likelihood ratio around this shared null law in powers of $\beta$. We prove that if the unknown parameter is first globally identifiable at order $r$ in this expansion, then estimation to fixed accuracy requires at least on the order of $\beta^{-2r}$ samples. We further identify a likelihood-separation stability condition that is necessary for any estimator to attain this rate and, under mild regularity conditions, sufficient for both maximum likelihood and method-of-moments estimators to attain it. We also study the regime in which the target accuracy vanishes together with the signal strength, and show that global localization and local refinement may be governed by different likelihood orders, leading to distinct statistical scales. Finally, we apply our framework to broad classes of algebraically structured latent-variable models, including additive-noise channels and exponential-family models.
item.dc:creator: Amnon Balanov, Tamir Bendory, Dan Edidin

item.title: Dimension-free comparison inequalities between $f$-divergences for Gaussian location mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2610.25070v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish dimension-free comparison inequalities between the Kullback-Leibler (KL) and $\chi^2$-divergences and the squared Hellinger distance for Gaussian location mixtures with compactly supported mixing distributions. We show that both divergences are bounded by the squared Hellinger distance up to constants depending only on the radius of the support, independently of the ambient dimension and the number of mixture components. These results resolve an open question raised by \cite{jia2023entropic} and strengthen existing comparison inequalities. Our proof relies on a Gaussian interpolation argument that relates the derivatives of these divergences to differences between posterior means.
item.dc:creator: Jeonghwan Lee, Cong Ma

item.title: LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction
item.description: arXiv:2610.25213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation relies on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECC). Of particular interest are codes that combine a high encoding rate with sufficient distance. Existing algebraic constructions, such as lifted product (LP) codes, build a large quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code from a classical base matrix. In this work we introduce LiftDiff, a generative approach to the discovery of QECC. A discrete denoising diffusion model is trained to generate base matrices over the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]$, which are then expanded into LP codes. The reverse diffusion process is guided by an energy function that evaluates quantum code properties, including girth, degree, sparsity and decoding performance, steering the sampler toward matrices that yield LP codes with favorable parameters. Our method discovers codes with parameters such as $[[169,13,11]]$, $[[143,15,9]]$, and $[[260,24,10]]$, including a $[[247,19,14]]$ code that achieves the highest ${kd^2}/{n}$ among the baselines. Moreover, several discovered codes outperform the Gross code across a broad range of the tested physical error rates under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise.
item.dc:creator: Yotam Peled, Eliya Nachmani

item.title: Can Quantum Entanglement Increase the Capacity of a Classical Relay Channel?
item.description: arXiv:2610.25334v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show positive and negative results on classical relay channels with entanglement assistance, revealing a sharp contrast between strictly causal and causal relay encoding. First, we consider van der Meulen's setting of a unit-delay relay, with strictly causal encoding. We show that the standard cutset upper bound continues to hold with entanglement assistance, and deduce that entanglement does not increase the capacity for several classes of relay channels. Second, we consider a zero-delay relay, where the encoding is causal. We present an example in which entanglement enables rates that exceed the cutset upper bound by at least 12.5%. Namely, entanglement shared between the source and relay significantly increases the capacity of a classical zero-delay relay channel.
item.dc:creator: Elsa Mizrahi, Uzi Pereg

item.title: Frobenius Profiles of Polynomial-Multiple MRD Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.25722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Frobenius intersection profiles of maximum rank distance (MRD) codes arising from ordinary polynomial multiples over finite fields. We prove that every numerically admissible profile is realized within this family over every sufficiently large extension, using a root-exponent pattern independent of the extension degree. A factor-orbit gap formula provides the underlying structural description, while effective extension-degree bounds guarantee realization. We also establish a lower bound valid for all polynomial generators and show that the upper and lower bounds differ by only $O_q(\log n)$ along an infinite family of parameters. Finally, we characterize the generalized Gabidulin members and obtain non-generalized-Gabidulin realizations of every profile with initial loss at least two over infinitely many extensions.
item.dc:creator: Yangcheng Li, Pingzhi Yuan

item.title: Neural Video Coding under Limited Delay: Theoretical Optimality and System Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.25729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditional neural video compression (NVC) methods predominantly follow strictly causal predictive-coding paradigm, treating zero-frame delay as a fixed constraint rather than delay as an explicit design parameter. From an information-theoretic perspective, allowing limited frame delay enables a codec to exploit correlations with future frames within the delay window, thereby reducing uncertainty that is inaccessible to strictly causal prediction and potentially improving the rate-distortion tradeoff. In this work, we formalize this intuition through a rigorous rate-distortion analysis builds on the clique factorization of Markov networks, and propose Graph-Factored Sequential Coding (GFSC), a principled framework for sequential video coding under limited delay. To our knowledge, we provide the first theoretical result showing that, for general $K$-order Markov sources with positive distributions, a $K$-frame delay is sufficient to attain joint-coding rate-distortion optimality over a nontrivial distortion region, a guarantee unavailable to zero-delay causal coding in general. In practice, we instantiate GFSC through lightweight neural modules, allowing existing causal predictive codecs to be augmented without modifying their core architectures. Experiments across multiple NVC models and datasets show that GFSC consistently improves rate-distortion performance over the corresponding causal counterparts. Under matched delay budgets, GFSC also achieves competitive performance compared with representative bidirectional codecs.
item.dc:creator: Likun Cai, Jun Chen, Ashish Khisti

item.title: Optimal Priors for Betting Tests with Bounded Payoffs: An Exact Efficiency Characterization
item.description: arXiv:2610.25821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Testing by betting is a powerful framework that recasts hypothesis testing as a betting game. A popular approach uses an $F$-weighted portfolio with a predefined prior $F$. For suitable priors, this approach has recently been shown to achieve the optimal expected rejection time as the error probability goes to zero at a fixed alternative. Yet, the prior $F$ changes how the portfolio test behaves near the null. This motivates the question: Which prior should we use in testing-by-betting algorithms? We study bounded scalar payoffs and introduce an efficiency measure that allows the error probability and alternative to vary jointly. Under mild assumptions, we prove that efficiency equals a logarithmic decay index of the prior near zero. This gives a necessary and sufficient condition for optimality: Beta priors have infinite efficiency, whereas suitable Robbins-type priors attain efficiency 1. As an application, we consider testing a specified mean of a bounded random variable and describe an implementation of the portfolio algorithm with almost-linear computational complexity.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Orabona

item.title: Waveguide Deployment Optimization for Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.26355v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most existing studies on pinching-antenna systems optimize the antenna positions or activation states under a prescribed waveguide deployment, where mutually parallel waveguides are commonly adopted. However, it remains unclear whether, and under what conditions, such a deployment is optimal from a communication-performance perspective. To fill this gap, this paper investigates long-term waveguide deployment optimization for pinching-antenna systems over a rectangular service region. We first consider the fundamental two-waveguide case and derive a closed-form sufficient condition, jointly determined by the waveguide height and the service-region aspect ratio, under which a deployment parallel to the longer side of the service region is globally optimal. We then consider the general multi-waveguide case, where the orientation and offset of each waveguide are jointly optimized without prescribing any deployment pattern, and develop an adaptive exchange algorithm for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. We further show that, within the parallel class, the waveguides should be aligned with the longer side of the service region, while in the large-height regime, the globally optimal unrestricted deployment asymptotically concentrates all waveguides on the centerline along the longer side. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithm and reveal how the preferred deployment geometry depends on the waveguide height and service-region shape. In particular, nonparallel deployments can provide noticeable gains in intermediate-height regimes, whereas parallel or center-concentrated deployments become favorable in other regimes.
item.dc:creator: Yanqing Xu, Zhiguo Ding, Xiu Yin Zhang, Tsung-Hui Chang

item.title: The binomial distribution maximises entropy among sums of negatively related indicators with fixed mean and support
item.description: arXiv:2610.26543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the binomial distribution supported on $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ and with mean $np$ for some $0<p<1$ maximises entropy within the class of sums of negatively related indicator random variables with this mean and support. Our results generalise the main result of Yu (2008), who showed that this binomial distribution maximises entropy within the smaller class of ultra-log-concave random variables of order $n$. Our proof makes use of a Markov chain construction of Yu (2008), together with a stochastic ordering argument.
item.dc:creator: Fraser Daly

item.title: DM-RSA-OAEP: Formal Treatment of a Dual-Modulus Fault-Detection Countermeasure Based on Physical Diversity
item.description: arXiv:2610.26642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit DM-RSA, an RSA variant that uses two independent moduli, whose original version was broken by H{\aa}stad's attack and contained an incorrect compromise-tolerance claim. We give a formal treatment of its repaired variant, DM-RSA-OAEP: (i) a complete IND-CCA2 security proof in the random-oracle model via a two-step hybrid argument, upper-bounding the security of the scheme by that of the weaker underlying RSA-OAEP instance, with an explicit simulation loss; (ii) a fault-detection theorem in an explicit adversary model that covers computation, key, and verification faults, including safe-error attacks, under a clearly stated physical-diversity assumption; (iii) an explicit analysis of why the countermeasure degrades to uselessness when the diversity assumption is violated (common-mode faults on a single chip). We position the scheme against the countermeasure landscape and against the broken dual-modulus literature. The contribution is deliberately framed as a fault countermeasure with a provable detection guarantee, not as a computationally stronger RSA. We conclude with a concrete instantiation and a detailed measurement protocol.
item.dc:creator: Ramamonjy Andriamifidisoa, Rufine Marius Lalasoa

item.title: Code Equivalence, Point Set Equivalence, and Polynomial Isomorphism
item.description: arXiv:2511.06843v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The linear code equivalence (LCE) problem is known to be equivalent to the point set equivalence (PSE) problem, i.e., the problem to check whether two sets of points in a projective space over a finite field differ by a linear change of coordinates. For such a point set $\mathbb{X}$, let $R$ be its homogeneous coordinate ring and $\mathfrak{J}_{\mathbb{X}}$ its canonical ideal. Then the LCE problem is shown to be equivalent to an algebra isomorphism problem for the doubling $R/\mathfrak{J}_{\mathbb{X}}$. As this doubling is an Artinian Gorenstein algebra, we can use its Macaulay inverse system to reduce the LCE problem to a Polynomial Isomorphism (PI) problem for homogeneous polynomials. The last step is polynomial time under some mild assumptions about the codes. Moreover, for indecomposable iso-dual codes we can reduce the LCE search problem to the PI search problem of degree 3 by noting that the corresponding point sets are self-associated and arithmetically Gorenstein, so that we can use the isomorphism problem for the Artinian reductions of the coordinate rings and form their Macaulay inverse systems.
item.dc:creator: Martin Kreuzer

item.title: Generative Site-Specific Beamforming for Next-Generation Spatial Intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2601.02301v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article proposes generative site-specific beamforming (GenSSBF) for next-generation spatial intelligence in wireless networks. Site-specific beamforming (SSBF) has emerged as a promising paradigm to mitigate the channel acquisition bottleneck in multiantenna systems by exploiting environmental priors. However, classical SSBF based on discriminative deep learning struggles: 1) to properly represent the inherent multimodality of wireless propagation and 2) to effectively capture the structural features of beamformers. In contrast, by leveraging conditional generative models, GenSSBF addresses these issues via learning a conditional distribution over feasible beamformers. By doing so, the synthesis of diverse and high-fidelity beam candidates from coarse channel sensing measurements can be guaranteed. This article presents the fundamentals, system designs, and implementation methods of GenSSBF. Case studies in both indoor and outdoor scenarios show that GenSSBF attains near-optimal beamforming gain with ultra-low channel acquisition overhead. Finally, several open research problems are highlighted.
item.dc:creator: Zhaolin Wang, Zihao Zhou, Cheng-Jie Zhao, Yuanwei Liu

item.title: Reed-Solomon Codes with Optimal Repair Bandwidth: A Basis-Transformation Approach
item.description: arXiv:2601.10685v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Maximum distance separable (MDS) codes are widely used in distributed storage, but naively repairing a single failure in an $(n,k)$ MDS code requires downloading the full contents of $k$ surviving nodes. Minimum storage regenerating (MSR) codes, introduced by Dimakis et al., minimize repair bandwidth while preserving the MDS property by contacting $d>k$ helper nodes and downloading only a fraction of each helper. For scalar MDS codes, Guruswami and Wootters established a linear repair framework, and Tamo, Ye, and Barg subsequently gave the first explicit Reed-Solomon (RS) codes achieving the MSR point. Their construction yields RS-MSR codes with subpacketization $\ell=s\prod_{i=1}^n p_i$, where $s=d+1-k$ and the distinct primes $p_i$ satisfy $p_i\equiv 1\pmod{s}$. In this paper, we show that this congruence condition is not intrinsic to the RS repair problem. We develop a basis-transformation approach to the construction of repair-enabling subspaces. The approach consists of three deterministic operations -- Euclidean Square Partition, Transposition, and Column Aggregation -- which construct the required repair-enabling subspaces directly from the standard monomial basis of the repair field. Consequently, we obtain RS-MSR codes with subpacketization $\ell=s\prod_{i=1}^n p_i$ for arbitrary distinct primes $p_i>s$. For fixed $s$, this improves the subpacketization of the Tamo--Ye--Barg construction by a factor asymptotic to $\varphi(s)^{n+\mathrm{o}(n)}$, where $\varphi(\cdot)$ denotes Euler's totient function.
item.dc:creator: Jing Qiu, Weijun Fang, Shu-Tao Xia, Fang-Wei Fu

item.title: Derivation Depth as an Information Metric: Axioms, Coding Theorems, and Storage--Computation Tradeoffs
item.description: arXiv:2602.19137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce derivation depth-a computable metric of the reasoning effort needed to answer a query based on a given set of premises. We model information as a two-layered structure linking abstract knowledge with physical carriers, and separate essential core facts from operational shortcuts. For any finite premise base, we define and prove the computability of derivation depth. By encoding reasoning traces and applying information-theoretic incompressibility arguments, we establish fundamental bounds linking depth to the descriptive complexity of queries. For frequently asked, information-rich queries, the minimal description length grows proportionally to depth times the logarithm of the knowledge base size. This leads to a practical storage-computation tradeoff: queries accessed beyond a critical threshold become cheaper to cache than recompute. We formulate optimal cache allocation as a mathematical optimization problem solvable with approximation guarantees and extend the framework to handle noisy or incomplete knowledge bases.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Qiua, Rui Wang*, Jianfeng Xu*

item.title: Insertion Correcting Capability for Quantum Deletion-Correcting Codes
item.description: arXiv:2602.20635v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is conjectured that a quantum code $C$ corrects $t$ deletion errors if and only if $C$ corrects a total of $t$ insertion and deletion errors. Although this conjecture has been proved only under certain conditions, it has not been proved in general. In this paper, we prove this conjecture for general quantum codes. Specifically, we show that a quantum state after an insertion error is represented as a product state of the original multi-qudit system and the inserted quantum state. Then, we prove this conjecture by combining the previous results and this property. In addition, we define generalized insertion errors by removing the quantum channel requirement from insertion errors and present their properties.
item.dc:creator: Ken Nakamura, Takayuki Nozaki

item.title: The Asymmetric Hamming Bidistance and Distributions over Binary Asymmetric Channels
item.description: arXiv:2604.07730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The binary asymmetric channel is a model for practical communication systems where the error probabilities for symbol transitions $0\rightarrow 1$ and $1\rightarrow0$ differ substantially. In this paper, we introduce the notion of asymmetric Hamming bidistance (AHB) and its two-dimensional distribution, which separately captures directional discrepancies between codewords. This finer characterization enables a more discriminative analysis of decoding the error probabilities for maximum-likelihood decoding (MLD), particularly when conventional measures, such as weight distributions and existing discrepancy-based bounds, fail to distinguish code performance. Building on this concept, we derive a new upper bound on the average error probability for binary codes under MLD and show that, in general, it is incomparable with the two existing bounds derived by Cotardo and Ravagnani (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 68 (5), 2022). To demonstrate its applicability, we compute the complete AHB distributions for several families of codes, including two-weight and three-weight projective codes (with the zero codeword removed) via strongly regular graphs and 3-class association schemes, as well as nonlinear codes constructed from symmetric balanced incomplete block designs (SBIBDs).
item.dc:creator: Shukai Wang, Cuiling Fan, Chunming Tang, Zhengchun Zhou

item.title: Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Nonlinear Control
item.description: arXiv:2604.20369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite-horizon rate-cost tradeoffs for general stochastic control systems, including nonlinear systems. Under an average control cost constraint, we show that the minimum expected communication rate lies within an additive logarithmic gap above the normalized directed information minimized over causal control policies. This establishes directed information as the operationally relevant quantity governing rate-limited control, extending its previously established roles in causal source coding and linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control to general nonlinear control systems.
item.dc:creator: Eray Unsal Atay, Venkat Chandrasekaran, Victoria Kostina

item.title: The Closure of LCD-to-GI Reductions via Generalized Inner Products
item.description: arXiv:2605.23120v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Permutation Equivalence Problem (PEP) for linear complementary dual (LCD) codes reduces to Graph Isomorphism (GI) through the orthogonal projector onto the code, but this requires a trivial hull. We ask whether the reduction extends when the standard inner product is replaced by a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form \(M\). We make precise what it means for \(M\) to yield a valid reduction to GI and prove that, for length \(n \geq 3\) and every field size, this holds if and only if \(M\) is permutation-invariant. The reduction then reaches, beyond LCD codes, a class of codes with one-dimensional hull: exactly those whose hull is spanned by a vector with nonzero coordinate sum. We count these codes exactly; for odd \(q\), asymptotically the method covers a fraction \(\prod_{i \geq 2}(1+q^{-i})^{-1}\) of all codes, \(1 + q^{-1}\) times the fraction of LCD codes. A polynomial-time reduction algorithm is given.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka

item.title: On the Role of Normalization in Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding for 1-bit Compressed Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2607.15530v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding (BIHT) is a simple, yet effective, greedy method for recovering a sparse vector from one-bit sign measurements. In its original form, BIHT performs a ``gradient-descent'' step, followed by hard thresholding. A convergence analysis of this algorithm was left open in the introductory work of Jacques, Laska, Boufounos, and Baraniuk [IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory (2013)] and has remained unresolved for over a decade, with subsequent sharp analyses studying a {\em normalized variant} instead, that additionally projects every iterate onto the unit sphere. This paper resolves that gap and characterizes when per-iteration normalization is algorithmically necessary. In the noiseless setting, we prove a universal, sample-optimal convergence theorem for the original BIHT algorithm. Specifically, with $\widetilde O(s/\epsilon)$ measurements, a deterministic, computable finite-time iterate has directional error at most $\epsilon$, simultaneously for every $s$-sparse unit vector. This matches the optimal sample dependence achieved by normalized BIHT in prior work. Under sign corruptions, we prove a sharp separation. If at most a $\tau$ fraction of signs are flipped adversarially, then BIHT, without per-iterate normalization, still reaches the robust error floor at an early iterate with a matching $\widetilde O(s/\epsilon)$ sample complexity rate as its normalized variant. This recovery, however, is not stable. We prove a scalar lower bound showing that any nontrivial corruption pattern, even one that involves only one flipped sign together with one clean sign, forces the iterates to oscillate indefinitely. Consequently, no general last-iterate convergence theorem can hold for BIHT under sign corruptions, while its normalized surrogate provably escapes this instance.
item.dc:creator: Arya Mazumdar, Prateeti Mukherjee

item.title: Cram\'er-Rao Bound Analysis for Cell-Free ISAC Systems with Fluid Intelligent Metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.16634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fluid intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) reshape antenna geometry to improve angular sensitivity. This paper studies their role in cell-free integrated sensing and communication, where distributed access points provide distinct observation directions. Under calibrated path gains, we derive the conditional angular Fisher information matrix, retain cross-AP coupling, and map it to a position-domain Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB). A diagonal-information specialization exposes the dependence on angular diversity, while a multi-target extension quantifies the loss from jointly estimating other target positions. We use CRB-driven coordinate search to design transmit and receive shapes and evaluate sensing performance, equal-resource AP scaling, and MRT-based communication--sensing allocation. In the considered four-Tx/four-Rx configuration, shape design reduces the position root CRB from 0.300 to 0.227 m at 10 dB reference SNR. Two-target results further illustrate how cross-target coupling increases the joint localization bound at small separations.
item.dc:creator: Changhao He, Jiguang He, Asmaa Abdallah, Ahmed M. Eltawil

item.title: Exact Rate Exponent Tradeoff for New Classes of Distributed Hypothesis Testing Problems
item.description: arXiv:2608.23465v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the optimal Stein error exponent for one-way distributed hypothesis testing under a communication rate constraint. We establish exact rate-exponent tradeoffs for new classes of finite-alphabet sources, including a complete single-letter characterization for every pair of strictly positive binary joint distributions as well as testing-against-dependence. Our converse analysis refines the auxiliary-receiver method through three complementary steps. First, we establish an information-projection identity that identifies the posterior-divergence optimization in an existing converse with Han's exponent functional. Second, we obtain an additional excess-rate branch by retaining a mutual-information term discarded in the usual rate relaxation. Third, we develop a two-telescope upper bound whose auxiliary variables are coupled through a joint rate constraint. Combining these bounds with information-geometric matching conditions yields exact exponents for three classes of sources by matching the achievable bounds of Han and Shimokawa-Han-Amari.
item.dc:creator: Zhenduo Wen, Amin Gohari, Mich\`ele Wigger

item.title: Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts
item.description: arXiv:2609.19493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We reduce the leading redundancy coefficient for binary codes correcting any fixed number $t\ge2$ of deletions from $2t$ to $2t-1$. This is the first improvement to that coefficient since Levenshtein's 1965 bound. More generally, over every fixed alphabet of size $q\ge2$, codes of length $n$ correcting any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions and substitutions exist with redundancy $(2t-1)\log_q n+O_t(\log_q\log_q n)$. For two deletions, the upper-bound coefficient drops from $4$ to $3$, halving the gap to the lower-bound coefficient $2$. The leading coefficient $2t-1$ also holds for $t$ bounded substring edits, where both the removed and inserted strings have bounded length. The proof combines random binary linear hashing of substring counts with a two-colouring argument. A linear dependence among differences of substring-count vectors forces their local changes to overlap, and this overlap lowers the redundancy coefficient from $2t$ to $2t-1$. The result provides an edit-distance analogue of Varshamov's 1957 bound in the Hamming metric, both in the leading redundancy coefficient and in the role of linear independence in the proof.
item.dc:creator: Eyal En Gad

item.title: Mutual Information Constrained Chernoff Bottleneck
item.description: arXiv:2609.37994v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical information bottleneck (IB) measures the relevance of a representation $U$ of $X$ to a target $Y$ by $I(U;Y)$, which does not directly characterize the error of downstream decisions. For a binary hypothesis $Y$ inferred from many separately encoded observations, the optimal error exponent is the Chernoff information between the two conditional distributions of $U$ given $Y$. We study the mutual information constrained Chernoff bottleneck, which seeks an encoder that maximizes this Chernoff information subject to a rate constraint $I(U;X) \leq R$. We show that its optimal value $C(R)$ increases strictly up to $R = H(V)$, where $V$ merges the symbols of $X$ with equal likelihood ratio, remains at the uncompressed exponent beyond, and, unlike the IB curve, need not be concave. We further show that $k+1$ outputs suffice to attain $C(R)$, where $k$ is the cardinality of $V$. We propose an alternating algorithm that updates the encoder via a generalized Blahut--Arimoto algorithm and the Chernoff parameter $s$ via a nonlinear equation, and prove that its iterates remain feasible, with nondecreasing and convergent Chernoff information. Comparing with the classical IB for $n$ samples, we show that, whenever the two objectives disagree, the IB encoder has the smaller equivocation $H(Y|U^{n})$ at $n = 1$, whereas the Chernoff bottleneck has the smaller error probability and equivocation for all large $n$. Numerical experiments confirm the theory, and on real topic-detection data from the 20 Newsgroups corpus, compressing each word to only $17\%$ of its entropy retains $90\%$ of the error exponent and nearly the accuracy of the uncompressed classifier.
item.dc:creator: Dier Tang, Guangyue Han

item.title: On the Information Bottleneck for Stable Variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.08007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a generalization of the Gaussian information bottleneck problem to jointly stable variables $X$ and $Y$. Specifically, for $X = Y + A$, where $A$ is stable and independent of $Y$, we find optimal stable linear encoders of the form $T = kX + N$, with $N$ stable and independent of $X$. We characterize the linear stable information bottleneck in closed-form and its critical value.
