Furthermore, we show that, except for the Gaussian case, such stochastic linear encoders are strictly suboptimal, while becoming asymptotically optimal at large compression rates. Our linear solution recovers the Gaussian information bottleneck for jointly Gaussian variables as a special case.
item.dc:creator: Dongmin Park, Jihad Fahs, Mohamad Assaad

item.title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
item.description: arXiv:2610.16707v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xinjie, Dier Tang, Shao-Lun Huang

item.title: Spatial Distribution of Mean PAoI in LEO Satellite-enabled IoT Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.23597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), such as Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, can provide consistent coverage for Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, particularly in rural areas where cellular coverage is lacking. These IoT nodes are used to monitor and record their surroundings, supporting various applications, including real-time applications. In such cases, transmission of the most up-to-date data is essential, making the Age of Information (AoI) a critical metric to consider. The AoI measures the elapsed time from the data generation at the source node to its reception at the destination. Moreover, the Peak AoI (PAoI), which denotes the maximum AoI in the system before an update is received, provides valuable insights into the network's performance. Therefore, this encourages us to focus on the PAoI within a large-scale and fully loaded IoT network, which is covered by LEOSATs. Using tools from stochastic geometry, this paper derives the spatial distribution of the uplink mean PAoI in a LEOSAT-enabled IoT network. To achieve that purpose, the meta distribution of the uplink conditional coverage probability is derived. Numerical results articulate how varying the number of deployed LEOSATs and their altitudes affects the coverage probability meta distribution and the spatial distribution of the mean PAoI. Additionally, by examining various scenarios with different numbers of LEOSATs and altitudes, we can derive valuable insights to determine the optimal beamwidth for LEOSATs tailored to each specific scenario to minimize the conditional mean PAoI.
item.dc:creator: Badiaa Gabr, Mustafa A. Kishk

item.title: A Linearly Convergent Algorithm for Petz-Augustin Means with Applications to Computing Petz-Augustin Capacity and Equilibrium Prices in Fisher Markets
item.description: arXiv:2502.06399v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the computation of the Petz-Augustin mean of order $\alpha \in (0,1) \cup (1,\infty)$, defined as the minimizer of a weighted sum of $n$ Petz-R\'enyi divergences of order $\alpha$ over the set of $d$-by-$d$ quantum states, where the Petz-R\'enyi divergence is a quantum generalization of the classical R\'enyi divergence. We propose the first algorithm with a non-asymptotic convergence guarantee for solving this optimization problem. The iterates are guaranteed to converge to the Petz-Augustin mean at a linear rate of $O\left( \lvert 1 - 1/\alpha \rvert^T \right)$ with respect to the Thompson metric for $\alpha\in(1/2,1)\cup(1,\infty)$, where $T$ denotes the number of iterations. The algorithm has an initialization time complexity of $O\left(nd^3\right)$ and a per-iteration time complexity of $O\left(nd^2 + d^3\right)$. Two applications follow. The first application concerns the Petz-Augustin capacity of order $\alpha\in(1/2,1)$, which generalizes the quantum channel capacity and characterizes the optimal error exponent in classical-quantum channel coding. To compute this quantity, we propose the first iterative method with a non-asymptotic convergence guarantee, which uses our algorithm for computing the Petz-Augustin mean as a subroutine. The second application concerns the equilibrium prices in Fisher markets with constant elasticity of substitution (CES) utilities. We establish that when all buyers have CES utilities of common elasticity, the equilibrium prices are equivalent to the Petz-Augustin mean when all quantum states commute. In this case, our proposed algorithm is a t\^{a}tonnement process \`{a} la Walras. We further extend the algorithm to inhomogeneous Fisher markets, where buyers have CES utilities with different elasticities, and prove a faster convergence rate than existing t\^{a}tonnement-type algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Neng Chu, Wei-Fu Tseng, Yen-Huan Li

item.title: Decentralized Decoding with Adaptive Local Combining for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2510.17445v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In existing literature, a two-stage architecture comprising of large-scale fading decoding (LSFD) at the central processing unit (CPU) and local combining at the access points (APs) is commonly deployed for uplink processing in scalable cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. However, centralized LSFD (c-LSFD) requires cross-AP channel statistics at the CPU and local combining uses schemes that either do not suppress interference optimally or result in analytically intractable solutions. We provide novel schemes to address both concerns. First, we propose the decentralized LSFD (d-LSFD) scheme that maximizes a surrogate signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio built only from local interference covariance statistics and identify covariance-action regime where it is equivalent to c-LSFD. Second, based on the fact that the antennas at each AP provide spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) for both interference suppression and coherent array gain, we interpret every combining scheme as solving the optimal DoF allocation problem over available DoFs. Selective zero-forcing (ZF) schemes solve this problem over both the dimension and composition of the local ZF subspace. We then provide the DoF-adaptive ZF-subspace (DAZS) combining scheme, which lets each AP select the optimal directions in the ZF subspace by maximizing its local sum spectral efficiency. Our numerical results establish the efficacy and efficiency of the proposed schemes compared to the corresponding existing schemes.
item.dc:creator: Mohd Saif Ali Khan, Karthik RM, Samar Agnihotri

item.title: Post-Selection Distributional Model Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2603.23055v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Formal model evaluation methods typically certify that a model satisfies a prescribed target key performance indicator (KPI) level. However, in many applications, the relevant target KPI level may not be known a priori, and the user may instead wish to compare candidate models by analyzing the full trade-offs between performance and reliability achievable at test time by the models. This task, requiring the reliable estimate of the test-time KPI distributions, is made more complicated by the fact that the same data must often be used both to pre-select a subset of candidate models and to estimate their KPI distributions, causing a potential post-selection bias. In this work, we introduce post-selection distributional model evaluation (PS-DME), a general framework for statistically valid distributional model assessment after arbitrary data-dependent model pre-selection. Building on e-values, PS-DME controls post-selection false coverage rate (FCR) for the distributional KPI estimates and we establish explicit conditions under which it is provably more sample efficient than a baseline method based on sample splitting. Experiments on synthetic data, text-to-SQL decoding with large language models, and telecom network performance evaluation demonstrate that PS-DME enables reliable comparison of candidate configurations across a range of reliability levels, supporting the statistically reliable exploration of performance--reliability trade-offs.
item.dc:creator: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone

item.title: Beyond the Flat-Spike: Adaptive Sparse CCA for Decaying and Unbalanced Signals
item.description: arXiv:2604.16435v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SCCA) is a fundamental statistical tool for identifying linear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-view data. While minimax theory establishes an optimal sample complexity scaling additively with the sparsity levels of the canonical vectors, computationally efficient algorithms typically suffer from a suboptimal multiplicative dependence. This computational-statistical gap is intrinsically tied to worst-case ``flat'' signal assumptions. In practice, however, multi-view signals frequently exhibit structured energy concentration, such as a power-law decay. To exploit this structural concentration and bypass the worst-case bottleneck, we propose Bilateral Spectral Energy Pursuit (Bi-SEP). Operating directly on the cross-covariance matrix, Bi-SEP is a stagewise adaptive algorithm that utilizes a proxy refinement step to dynamically track and capture cross-view signal energy. Theoretically, we establish a profile-adaptive sample complexity bound governed by the coupled energy profiles of the two views. Notably, under power-law decay models, we reveal a synergistic phase transition: the optimal linear sample complexity is attainable provided that the aggregate decay rate of the two views is sufficiently large. This result demonstrates that a highly concentrated signal in one view allows the model to accommodate a completely flat signal in its partner. Numerical experiments validate our theoretical findings, illustrating the advantages of Bi-SEP in structured, non-flat signal regimes.
item.dc:creator: Mengchu Xu, Jian Wang, Yonina C. Eldar

item.title: The Causal Description Gap: Information-Theoretic Separations Across Pearl's Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2605.02177v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pearl's causal hierarchy shows that observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries are qualitatively distinct. We ask a quantitative version of this question: how many additional bits are needed to specify higher-rung causal answers once lower-rung answers are known? We formalize this via query-class description length, the Kolmogorov complexity of the answers a structural causal model (SCM) gives to a class of queries, with system size given. Our main construction gives acyclic SCMs on $n$ binary variables whose common observational distribution has constant description length, while single-variable intervention answers can require $\Theta(n^2)$ additional bits. For SCMs with independent noises, fixed finite gate-schema and noise libraries, and at most $d$ parents per variable, a degree-sensitive upper bound gives an observational-interventional gap of at most $O(nd\log(en/d)+n\log n)$. This makes the quadratic construction order-optimal in the dense regime and a rooted-tree construction order-optimal for bounded indegree. The quadratic separation persists under $\varepsilon$-accurate total-variation descriptions for every fixed $\varepsilon<1/4$. At the next rung, even knowing every hard-intervention distribution can leave a $\Theta(n)$ counterfactual description gap; a masked-parity construction extends this to $\Theta(n^2)$. These separation rates hold in the worst case and with high probability under uniform hidden parameters. A general ambiguity-to-bits theorem and Shannon analogue, together with explicit encodings, show that the gaps in our constructions equal the logarithm of residual higher-rung ambiguity up to lower-order terms.
item.dc:creator: Seyed Morteza Emadi

item.title: All-out Attack: Optimal Block Withholding Under Pay-Per-Share Scheme
item.description: arXiv:2607.01209v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Classical Block Withholding (BWH) attacks have been extensively studied in block-dependent reward schemes, where pool members are compensated upon a block discovery within the pool. However, most contemporary mining pools operate under share-based schemes, wherein participants are paid immediately upon submission of valid shares. In this paper, we analyze BWH under Pay-Per-Share (PPS) for Nakamoto-style blockchains and prove that these mechanisms are not incentive compatible, contrary to conclusions drawn under fixed difficulty in prior literature. Under PPS, the optimal strategy for a BWH attacker is the All-out Attack (AoA): the adversary allocates its entire hashpower toward the victim pool, submitting only partial Proof-of-Work shares (pPoW) while withholding all valid blocks, i.e., full Proof-of-Work (fPoW). Prior to the first difficulty adjustment, the adversary incurs negligible loss from withheld fPoWs. After the adjustment reduces block difficulty, the adversary either generates more pPoWs per unit time when the pPoW difficulty is reduced accordingly or, if the pPoW difficulty is held fixed, earns a higher reward per share. In both cases, it achieves a post-adjustment reward rate of $\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}$ per target epoch, compared with the honest baseline rate of $\alpha$. Remarkably, this gain matches the theoretical upper bound achieved by optimal selfish mining in Nakamoto consensus under perfect network influence. The results further indicate that BWH is substantially more profitable under PPS than under mainstream block-dependent payout schemes, even when compared with advanced BWH variants. Honest miners benefit at the same rate as the adversary per unit hashpower, while the victim pool operator bears all losses, paying out-of-pocket for pPoW submissions without receiving fPoW compensation in return.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Doger, Sennur Ulukus

item.title: Reduced APN permutations and a disproof of the Galois-ring lifting conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.30808v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct infinite families of reduced almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations of $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$ that admit coefficientwise permutation lifts to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ for every $k>1$. These families disprove Conjecture~2 of R\o njom and Sandrib (Cryptogr. Commun., 2026), even for reduced polynomial representatives. For every odd $m\ge5$ with $3\nmid m$, we obtain explicit seven-term polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with formal derivative identically one. We derive them from a complete criterion for the reduced representative of $A(x)^{2^s+1}$ to have no critical point in $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$, where $A$ is an invertible linearized polynomial and $\gcd(s,m)=1$. We then apply the cube case to construct a second family of degree $2^{m-1}+2$, whose nonconstant derivatives avoid zero by an explicit trace identity. A fixed parameter in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ gives this family in every dimension $m=5r$ with $r$ odd, including a degree-$18$ example over $\mathbb{F}_{32}$. Both constructions remain in Gold linear equivalence classes, so liftability of reduced representatives is not invariant under invertible $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear input changes. We obtain the lifting conclusions from the standard Galois-ring permutation criterion. We also verify a degree-$24$ example supplied by Zhang and Haobo, prove a trace-adjoint criterion for reduced quadratic functions, and interpret the derivative condition through ramification at rational points.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Pantelimon Stanica

item.title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
item.description: arXiv:2609.30159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to establish code families with constant encoding rate and linear distance, simultaneously achieving optimal asymptotic scaling in both parameters. In particular, we characterize explicit logical representatives of the full gauged code space, and provide a fundamental treatment of non-Abelian code distance in the sense of Knill--Laflamme based on combining expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary errors. We further construct an almost-good family with entire code spaces exhibiting long-range magic. Moreover, we use linearly addressable cup product to directly generate linearly many encoded magic states from gauging measurements of Clifford operators. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting, lay the foundation for pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture and shed light on non-Abelian quantum phases and orders beyond geometric locality.
item.dc:creator: Zimu Li, Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Zi-Wen Liu

item.title: Undirected Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages. Fractional routing instead splits each message among source-destination paths and forwards its parts without combining different messages. For undirected networks carrying independent messages between multiple source-destination pairs, the multiple-unicast conjecture asserts that the two methods achieve the same combinations of message rates. We give a finite counterexample and use its linear structure to accelerate external-memory integer sorting, addressing the question of whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound posed by Aggarwal and Vitter in 1988. We give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $\Theta(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is $O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon}\right]\right)$, where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. In some parameter ranges, this bound is asymptotically smaller than the classical comparison-sorting bound. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Baochun Li, Zongpeng Li, Sirui Liu

item.title: Hankel Submatrices with Bounded Word Length: Dimension Tradeoffs in Probabilistic and Quantum Automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.21797v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize the largest admissible side length of fixed-margin square Hankel submatrices generated by probabilistic realizations on a \(d\)-point carrier and quantum linear realizations on a \(d\)-dimensional Hilbert space, when prefix and suffix word lengths are bounded by \(T\). Using a four-symbol transition alphabet shared by all selected rows and columns, we show that, for fixed margins \(\lambda_2>0\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2<1\), the corresponding side lengths satisfy \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d^2,T\})\) for completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) quantum realizations and \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d,T\})\) for probabilistic automata. Four unitary and four permutation transition maps attain the corresponding orders. At zero false-acceptance tolerance (\(\lambda_2=0\) with \(0\leq\lambda_1<1\)), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=\Theta(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). The upper bounds follow from state-space packing and word counting, while the lower bounds combine explicit transition tuples with Grassmannian and positive-rate codebooks whose existence follows from the probabilistic method. These results establish sharp dimension--word-length tradeoffs for bounded-word Hankel tables.
